one_liner: Close is a CRM with a broad REST API, OAuth 2.0 and API keys, webhooks and an official MCP server. Getting credentials needs a Close org. The pages show no free plan or trial, only free secondary orgs and manually requested Dev orgs.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 is offered through creating an OAuth app, and the docs strongly recommend it for multi-user integrations. API keys are generated in Settings > Developer > API Keys and are tied to a user and organization. Access level is read-only or read/write/delete per key. The draft's BASIC was dropped because no fetched page mentions HTTP Basic. The real scheme may use key-as-username Basic, which is unverified here.
access_notes: The pages say nothing about a free plan or a trial, so the draft's self_serve_trial is unsupported. A Close org is needed to create API keys or an OAuth app. Existing Close users can create a free secondary organization. Non-users who are integration partners can email support for a free Dev organization, which is a manual step. Whether a self-serve trial exists is not settled by these pages.
blocker_notes: A Close organization is required. The pages confirm free secondary orgs for existing users and free Dev orgs by emailing support, but no self-serve free tier or trial. The paid-plan or trial path is unverified.

evidence.quote: Strongly recommended for user-facing integrations that multiple users will authenticate to.
A key is tied to a specific user and organization.
To create a new API key, go to **Settings > Developer > API Keys** and click **+ New API Key**.
You can create a free secondary organization.
Dev organizations work identically to standard Close organizations but have no subscription fees.
supports everything from a simple internal script to a full product integration used by thousands of Close customers.
Give Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other tools direct access to Close data via the [MCP server](https://developer.close.com/mcp) — no code required.
